title: Vinegar to Nylon: Uses of Carboxylic Acids
subject: Chemistry
objective: Where carboxylic acids are used: formic acid in industry, acetic acid as a solvent and vinegar, adipic acid for nylon-6,6 through amide links, sodium benzoate as a food preservative, fatty-acid salts as soap, and aspirin as a medicine.

fill.q: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ____ acid.
Sodium benzoate is used as a food ____.
Nylon-6,6 is made from hexamethylenediamine and ____ acid.
Soap is the sodium salt of a long-chain ____ acid.

tf.q: Formic acid is used in the leather and electroplating industries.
tf.explain: NCERT lists rubber, textile, dyeing, leather and electroplating.

tf.q: In nylon-6,6 the units are joined by ester links.
tf.explain: They are joined by amide links –CO–NH–.

ar.r: Its non-polar tail dissolves grease and its ionic head stays in water.

ar.a: Adipic acid can form a long polymer chain with a diamine.
ar.r: It has a –COOH group at each end.

short.q: Explain how an amide link forms between a –COOH group and an –NH₂ group.
short.solution: The N lone pair attacks the carbonyl carbon; water is lost; –CO–NH– forms.
